wing: 41st Combat Bombardment Wing (lead group, per 303rd BG mission report table)
dispatched_note: 303rd BG Combat Mission No. 78 report (14 Oct 1943) gives the 1st Air Division composition: 41st CBW lead 379BG (17), high 303BG (19), low 384BG (16); wing led by Col. Rohr. The figure is a single source and may be planned rather than actual; aborts not established.
lost_note: Six 379th aircraft with MACRs 954, 955, 956, 957, 958 and 1353 per the b17flyingfortress.de Schweinfurt loss table and aircraft histories (Freeman-derived). No 379th BG primary list was found to confirm the total; 42-3056's history text also says "Anklam" (see that record). 42-29870 (MACR 1038) appears under the 379th in the loss table but flew with the 384th BG on 14 Oct 1943 per 384th BG loading lists - excluded.

aircraft.loss_details: Shot down by enemy aircraft; crashed near Singhofen, 12 miles SW of Limburg, Germany (i.e. on the route, before the target). All 10 KIA.
aircraft.notes: Aircraft 527BS [FO-R]; history notes the crew was a 524BS crew ("Matt Zack {+ 524BS crew}"). CONFLICT: the source history text reads "Missing in Action Anklam 14/10/43" - Anklam was attacked on 9 Oct 1943; the date 14/10/43, the b17flyingfortress.de Schweinfurt loss table, and the MACR number (955, in the 954-958 run for the 379th on 14 Oct) indicate Schweinfurt. Recorded as a 14 Oct loss with this caveat.

aircraft.nickname_note: Freeman history ends "LADY ASTRID"; with the 95th BG it was "SPOOK II" [ET-K]. Which name it carried on 14 Oct 1943 is not established.
aircraft.loss_details: Attacked by fighter, bail-out ordered; flak burst destroyed the waist; aircraft exploded after four men bailed out (co-pilot Holtsberg statement). Fell out of formation at 14:55 after leaving Schweinfurt and crashed in a forest near Dornheim (near Iphofen, about 45 km S of Schweinfurt) per German observer and MACR 954 / KU 367 coordinates as analysed by b17flyingfortress.de; Freeman history says "Limburger Forest, near Dornheim, W of Darmstadt". 6 KIA, 4 POW.
aircraft.notes: Ex-95th BG (336BS ET-K "SPOOK II"); to 527BS/379BG [FO-E] 22 Jun 1943, then 524BS [WA-E]. German loss document KU 367. b17flyingfortress.de says a crew photo was taken 11 Oct 1943.

aircraft.notes: UNVERIFIED participant: a web-search summary of the 379th BG memorial/marker (hmdb.org, page returned HTTP 403) associated "Paddy Gremlin" with the 2nd Schweinfurt mission 14 Oct 43. Aircraft later lost 30 Jan 1944 (Brunswick). Participation, crew and outcome on 14 Oct 1943 not established.

research_gaps: No 379th BG loading list, sortie list, mission report or formation chart for 14 Oct 1943 found online. 379thbga.org has an expired TLS certificate; its plain-http and archived pages contain only a mission-date list (pdfs/missionreports.pdf), crew photos and reunion material.
Only the six losses are identified; the ~11 aircraft that returned (and any aborts) are unidentified - serials, pilots and crews UNKNOWN.

Crew lists come from one secondary source (b17flyingfortress.de, largely Freeman's "B-17 Fortress Story" history text derived from MACRs); MACRs 954-958 and 1353 themselves were not consulted (NARA/Fold3). Most names are informal short forms and most ranks are unknown.
americanairmuseum.com and hmdb.org returned HTTP 403; only search-result summaries used.
Squadron codes are each aircraft's 379th code from its service history, not confirmed for the date.
Group mission number for the 379th not established (the archived 379thbga.org mission list PDF is garbled).
